neighbours.label: a word that opens a fixed restrictive or correlative frame ('not only ... but', 'nothing but', 'nothing more than', 'something along the lines of'), as against the same words used as plain negation or pronouns
fire: Good teaching requires not only patience but also a sense of humour.
The famous cure was nothing but salt water with a little lemon.
The town's name means something along the lines of 'place by the ford'.
Her success came not only from talent but from years of practice.
Experts say the ghost photo is nothing more than a trick of the light.
The village offers visitors not only hiking but also fine local cheese.
His excuse was nothing but a story to avoid the meeting.
Call it something along the lines of 'Project Blue' for now.
quiet: Good teaching did not happen overnight in our small school.
The famous cure was sold in tiny bottles at the fair.
The town's name is painted on a sign by the old ford.
Her success did not surprise anyone who knew her family.
Experts say the ghost photo was taken in an old house.
The village does not have a bus stop or a shop.
His excuse was that the train had been cancelled again.
We heard nothing from them, so we named it 'Project Blue' ourselves.
